jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer, Amazon Leo Satellite Broadband Terminals
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.

What You'll Work On

Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

Key job responsibilities

What We Look For

Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware.
Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it.
Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system.

Our Stack

Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

A day in the life

As part of our Amazon Leo CT SW Team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Kuiper products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues.

About The Team

The Amazon Leo CT SW Team supports the devices that connect our customers to the Kuiper network. We provide software for both applications and the underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer, Amazon Leo Satellite Broadband Terminals
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.

What You'll Work On

Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

Key job responsibilities

What We Look For

Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware.
Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it.
Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system.

Our Stack

Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life

As part of our BSP software engineering team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Kuiper products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues.

About The Team

The Kuiper Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect our customers to the Kuiper network. We provide software for both applications and the underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.

jobs.description:
Software Developer (ASP.NET / WCAG Accessibility / Application Modernization)

Location:
Anaheim, California
Position Type:
Contract

Onsite

Skill sets /keywords :
Microsoft ASP.NET / .NET Framework 4.5+ , C#, ASP.NET MVC, HTML5, CSS / CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, AngularJS, Telerik / Kendo UI, Bootstrap 3.x, AJAX

Software Developer – ASP.NET / WCAG Accessibility / Application Modernization

Location:
Anaheim, California
Position Type:
Contract
Initial Contract:
3–6 months
Potential Extension:
12–24 months
Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Software Developer / Web Application Engineer
for an initial 3–6 month contract engagement focused on the WCAG 2.1 Level AA remediation of two existing public-facing web applications
built on the Microsoft ASP.NET platform.
The initial phase of the project requires working within an established legacy application stack to identify, remediate, test, and document accessibility issues while preserving existing application functionality and business workflows.
Following successful completion of the accessibility phase, this position has the potential to extend into a 12–24 month application modernization and re-engineering project
. The second phase will involve redesigning and rebuilding the existing applications using the current Microsoft .NET / ASP.NET Core web application stack.
This is an excellent opportunity for a developer who is comfortable working in both worlds: maintaining and improving an established production system today while helping architect its replacement for tomorrow.

Phase 1 – WCAG 2.1 Level AA Remediation

The initial 3–6 month engagement will focus primarily on accessibility remediation of two production, public-facing web applications.
Responsibilities will include:
Review existing ASP.NET web applications for WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance issues.
Remediate accessibility issues throughout the user interface while minimizing changes to existing business functionality.
Correct HTML structure, forms, labels, navigation, tables, dialogs, validation messages, and interactive controls.
Implement proper ARIA attributes and accessible markup where appropriate.
Improve keyboard navigation, tab order, focus management, and visible focus behavior.
Address color contrast, responsive layout, text scaling, and other accessibility requirements.
Improve compatibility with screen readers and assistive technologies.
Remediate accessibility issues involving third-party UI components, including Kendo UI.
Work with existing JavaScript and AngularJS components without unnecessarily destabilizing the production application.
Perform regression testing to ensure accessibility changes do not impact existing functionality.
Assist with accessibility testing using automated and manual testing techniques.
Document remediation changes, technical limitations, and any remaining accessibility exceptions.
Work directly with the existing development team to troubleshoot and resolve application issues.

Existing Technology Stack

Candidates should have hands-on experience with several of the following technologies:
Microsoft ASP.NET / .NET Framework 4.5+
C#
ASP.NET MVC
HTML5
CSS / CSS3
JavaScript
jQuery
AngularJS
Telerik / Kendo UI
Bootstrap 3.x
AJAX
REST / Web APIs
Microsoft Visual Studio
Git or equivalent source-control systems

Experience maintaining and modifying legacy production ASP.NET applications
is particularly important.
Accessibility Experience

Strong knowledge of web accessibility is highly desirable, including experience with:
WCAG 2.1 Level AA
WAI-ARIA
Semantic HTML
Keyboard-only navigation
Focus management
Accessible forms and validation
Screen-reader compatibility
Color contrast requirements
Responsive and zoom-compatible interfaces
Accessibility testing tools such as Axe, WAVE, Lighthouse, Accessibility Insights, or similar tools

Experience performing accessibility remediation on complex data-driven web applications
, rather than only static websites, is strongly preferred.
Phase 2 – Application Modernization

Candidates who successfully complete the initial remediation project may be offered an additional 12–24 month contract
to participate in the complete re-engineering of the two applications.
The modernization effort is expected to include:
Re-engineering legacy ASP.NET applications onto the current Microsoft .NET LTS platform.
Development using modern ASP.NET Core architecture.
Migration of legacy business logic and application functionality.
Modernization of the front-end architecture and user experience.
Replacement of legacy AngularJS and Bootstrap components with a modern supported front-end framework and component architecture.
Development of RESTful APIs and service-oriented application components.
Modern authentication and authorization.
Integration with Microsoft Azure services where appropriate.
Improved application security, maintainability, performance, scalability, and deployment.
Accessibility designed into the new application architecture rather than added afterward.
Preservation and validation of existing business rules during migration.
Participation in technical design, architecture, development, testing, and production deployment.

The modernization project will essentially move the applications from a legacy architecture that has accumulated years of dependencies into a modern, maintainable platform designed for the next generation of the system.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of professional software development experience preferred.
Strong C# and Microsoft ASP.NET development experience.
Strong HTML, CSS, and JavaScript skills.
Experience troubleshooting and modifying existing production web applications.
Understanding of browser developer tools and front-end debugging.
Ability to work within an existing codebase before proposing major architectural changes.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
Ability to independently analyze technical issues and implement production-quality solutions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to document technical changes and development decisions.

Highly Desirable Qualifications

Experience with any of the following is a significant plus:
WCAG 2.1 AA remediation
Government or public-sector web applications
ASP.NET MVC
AngularJS
Telerik Kendo UI
Bootstrap 3.x
Modern ASP.NET Core
Current .NET LTS releases
Entity Framework / Entity Framework Core
Microsoft SQL Server
Azure SQL
Microsoft Azure
Azure App Service
Azure DevOps
Git
CI/CD pipelines
Application migration from .NET Framework to modern .NET
Modern JavaScript or TypeScript frameworks

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a hands-on senior developer
who is comfortable opening an older application, understanding how it works, and improving it without assuming that everything must immediately be rewritten.
For the first phase, we need someone who can work carefully inside the existing engine while it is running
.
For the second phase, we need someone capable of helping us design and build the replacement engine using the modern Microsoft technology stack
.
Candidates with experience spanning both legacy Microsoft web development and modern .NET application architecture will be especially well suited for this engagement.
Contract Structure

Initial Engagement:

3–6 months focused primarily on WCAG 2.1 Level AA remediation and related application development.
Extension Opportunity:

Successful candidates may be considered for an additional 12–24 month engagement focused on application modernization and re-engineering.

Learn more about CaptiveAire and our products here

provides market leading property & casualty, accident & health, specialty and standard commercial lines insurance solutions. Since 2000, Crum & Forster’s Accident & Health division (A&H) has offered a diverse portfolio of specialty insurance and reinsurance products nationwide. We place a strong focus on product development and creative distribution methods, along with excellent client service and support.

Design, develop, and maintain full-stack applications using React, Angular, ASP.NET Core, .NET Core, and EF Core.

jobs.description:
About The Team

DoorDash is building the world’s most reliable on-demand logistics engine for delivery! We’re looking for experienced engineers to join our fast-growing engineering team to help us develop a 24x7 global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash’s three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers.

About The Role

At DoorDash, our product engineers implement and operate technological solutions to improve the experiences of our merchants, dashers, and consumers. From creating beautiful, user-friendly flows to crafting scalable backend architectures, we strive to deliver reliant, performant technology that delights our customers.

We believe interns are essential to our mission of attracting and retaining top talent. During our 12-week Software Engineer internship, interns are completely immersed in their teams and will have the opportunity to develop, maintain, and ship products. As an intern, you will directly impact our business by collaborating with your team to solve real problems for our customers.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. to be considered for this position. F-1 students are eligible if they are using Curricular Practical Training (CPT). DoorDash does not support students on J-1 visas at this time.

The 2027 internship program will be hosted in person at a Doordash office in one of the following locations; New York, San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Los Angeles and Seattle. You will have an opportunity to select your preferred location(s) during the application process.

You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…

Develop, maintain and ship technical elements with the support of your mentor, manager, and team members
Act on feedback, coaching, and mentorship from your mentor and team members
Actively learn about the elements to which you contribute
Make a direct impact on our business by collaborating with your team to solve problems for our customers
Participate in intern programming - Leadership Speaker series, social events – virtually and in-person
Present your summer learnings during a final presentation at the end of the internship
You are excited about an in person summer work experience

You have experience working with databases (e.g., AWS, SQL, etc.)
You have a solid understanding of algorithms and data structures

Experience with solutions for systems monitoring, live deployments, and continuous integration

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See Below For Paid Time Off Details

For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado.

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

As a Software Development Engineer at Micron you will configure, develop, test, maintain and support Micron and third party applications. You will create and analyze software specifications, and research, design, document, modify, test, and support software throughout the development life cycle. You can demonstrate the functional and technical skills necessary to switch between development technologies and merge them to deliver the best solution. You have a proven ability to create quality software and participate in quality improvement efforts. You will provide solutions that create business value while at the same time minimizing negative impact through defects, downtime, or performance degradation.

Responsibilities

Coordinate tool automation and host enhancements by partnering with automation developers and domain experts to deliver projects on schedule
Gather, prioritize, and document requirements for new automation systems and enhancements across 300mm fabs globally
Test and support manufacturing and automation software releases, including upgrades and resiliency improvements
Fix and resolve automation and software issues in a daily support role, including 24x7 on-call rotation
Maintain user documentation and provide regular project status reporting to management

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field with 5+ years of enterprise software development experience.
Hands-on experience with object-oriented programming, software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, and Agile/Scrum methodologies.
Experience using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.
Software testing experience within manufacturing or automation environments.
Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting or integrating automation systems in a semiconductor or manufacturing environment
Knowledge of software architecture, system integration, and automation tool frameworks
Experience crafting user documentation and training materials for software releases
Proven ability to solve complex software and automation issues across multiple systems
Experience supporting global or multi-site operations with standardized reporting and metrics

As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future. We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget. Micron also provides benefit programs that help protect your income if you are unable to work due to illness or injury, and paid family leave. Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays. For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits.

Micron is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, citizenship status, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

To learn about your right to work click here.

To learn more about Micron, please visit micron.com/careers

For US Sites Only: To request assistance with the application process and/or for reasonable accommodations, please contact Micron’s People Organization at hrsupport_na@micron.com or 1-800-336-8918 (select option #3)

Micron Prohibits the use of child labor and complies with all applicable laws, rules, regulations, and other international and industry labor standards.

Micron does not charge candidates any recruitment fees or unlawfully collect any other payment from candidates as consideration for their employment with Micron.

jobs.description:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Your Future Org

Atlassian’s Intern program combines hands-on technical training, professional growth opportunities, dedicated mentorship, and strong social connections. This holistic approach empowers students to hit the ground running and sets them up for a successful and impactful career at Atlassian!

This is a hybrid role located in Seattle, WA or San Francisco, CA. You must be willing and able to work out of Seattle or San Francisco to qualify.

This position is not eligible for F1 and J1 students. It is not available for any work sponsorship.

Our paid internship program runs for 12 weeks between May/June - August/September 2027.

Responsibilities

From day one, you will be a valued part of our development team, trusted to make changes to code that directly impact our products, while gaining deep technical knowledge in full lifecycle product development. You will report to Senior Engineers on your team and dream up and code new features that can be shipped straight into our products.

As part of a unified R&D team, Engineering is prioritizing key initiatives which support our customers in moving to cloud while simultaneously continuing to bring the most value to our customers through investments across our core product suite – including Jira, Confluence, Trello, and Bitbucket.

Performing as part of an Agile Scrum development team (5-10 member) that uses modern C++ for the development of Radio Frequency (RF) emitter products and solutions

Participating in the software project-level testing strategy and coordinating with the testing team to ensure new features are thoroughly tested
Participating in on-site customer integration efforts and test events
Assisting with software reviews to ensure software meets desired quality standards, is free from bugs, and behaves as intended
Mentoring junior software engineers to facilitate skill and knowledge development through informal opportunities, such as coaching or offering advice, and formal training opportunities

Minimum of a bachelor's degree in engineering or computer science and at least ten years' work-related experience or a master's degree in engineering or computer science and eight years' work-related experience or a Ph.D. in a relevant technical discipline or an equivalent combination of education and experience
Must have a strong background in Software Engineering activities to include research, design, development, debugging, integration, testing, and deployment
Must have experience leading a software development team

Must have a good understanding of parallelism, concurrency, or threading in a distributed environment
Must have a good working knowledge of build systems such as Make and CMake

Must have strong written and verbal communication skills
Must have good interpersonal skills and be capable of conflict resolution in a team environment

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Code Quality
jobs.description:
About The Team

The Code Quality team sits within the Developer Platform organization and owns the systems that keep DoorDash's codebase healthy and secure as it scales: static analysis, quality gates, test frameworks, regression infrastructure, and tooling. Our job is to make sure the signals engineers rely on before shipping — test results, coverage, performance feedback etc — are fast and trustworthy. The decisions we make about tooling and standards directly shape how confidently and quickly engineering teams at DoorDash can ship to production.

About The Role

We're looking for Software Engineers to help build and maintain the systems that validate code quality across DoorDash's engineering org, treating our tooling as a critical product for the engineers who rely on it every day: static analysis and quality gates, test frameworks and regression infrastructure. You’ll design the tooling and automation that will help derive trustworthy quality signals, integrate them into the development lifecycle, and make it easy for engineers to execute reliable, repeatable workflows. You will collaborate across the engineering org, partnering directly with the teams who use what you build to understand the accuracy, reliability and performance of their functionality. You will report into the Engineering Manager on our Code Quality team in our Developer Platform organization. You must be located in either San Francisco, CA, Sunnyvale, CA, Los Angeles, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY.

You're Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…

Build and maintain quality tooling — static analysis, quality gates, coverage reporting, test frameworks, regression infrastructure — and integrate it directly into our developer workflows and CI/CD pipelines
Define and derive quality signals - flakiness, pass rate, coverage, performance, scale readiness etc -
Build tooling that improves everyday engineering workflows, including local development, CI/CD, debugging, and rollouts
Explore how AI agents and tools can automate parts of building quality checks, and use real engineering usage data to measure their impact
Partner directly with engineering, product, and QA teams across DoorDash to find their biggest bottlenecks and ship tooling that demonstrably improves them

We're Excited About You Because…

Have experience building software quality infrastructure, test automation, meaningful ownership of build systems, CI/CD infrastructure, or developer productivity tooling
You have a strong debugging track record and have shipped changes that measurably improved an engineering team's workflow
You communicate clearly and partner effectively across functions — with engineers, product managers, and QA — to understand and solve real problems
You're comfortable working through ambiguous, cross-team problems and taking them to a solution with minimal guidance
You have proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See Below For Paid Time Off Details

For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado.

$159,800—$235,000 USD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

jobs.title: Software Test Engineer II
jobs.description:
About Us

At CNH, we're driven by a clear purpose: we serve and advance the people who feed and build a growing world.

As a global leader in agriculture and construction, we create the equipment, technology, and solutions that help our customers work more productively and sustainably. Our success starts with our people, and we foster a collaborative culture where innovation thrives and every employee has the opportunity to grow.

Grow a Career. Build a Future.

If you're ready to make an impact and build a career with purpose, there's a place for you at CNH.

Job Purpose

The Software Development Engineer in Test II
is a hands-on technical contributor on a team that collectively owns our automated test framework for embedded software running on the precision field computer platform. You'll help design, build, and scale that framework while developing robust automated test cases from system requirements, validating CAN bus and network communications, and ensuring compliance with industry standards including ISO 11783 (ISOBUS), SAE J1939, ISO 25119, and NMEA 2000. This work forms the automated safety net that lets our software teams ship with confidence.

Key Responsibilities

Evaluate test requirements, based on specifications, standard procedures, and internal/external requirements.
Design, create and run automated test cases, based on the requirements created.
Develop test plans and procedures.
Execute and document tests.
Identify and recommend test equipment, production equipment, fixturing, or tooling needed to meet product specifications.
Prepare reports of testing data, evaluate, and provide recommendations based on findings. Lead or contribute input for improvements.
Train team members on utilization of test equipment and procedures.
Keep abreast of new developments in the fields of engineering design, methods, and applications.
May assist with the request for quote process, as related to needs for the testing function.

Experience Required

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or technical field.
3+ years of engineering experience in Software Test Automation for Embedded systems.
Strong Proficiency in Python with 3+ years of experience for test case development and automation.
Hands-on Experience with CAN tools similar to CANoe/CANalyzer by Vector.
Experience with Qt/QML/Squish or equivalent GUI automation tools.
Familiarity with virtualization/emulation environments.
Understanding of Network Protocols and standards such as but not limited to: ISO11783 (ISOBUS), J1939
Experience with git and supporting CI/CD tools.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Linux and Build System/project Frameworks such as Yocto.
Background in Agricutural Embedded Systems.
Strong Communication and Problem-Solving skills.
Demonstrated use of Root-Cause Analysis tools (Five Whys, Ishikawa Diagrams, Fault-Tree, etc.)

Pay Transparency

The annual salary for this role is $86,625 - $132,825 plus any applicable bonus (Actual salaries will vary and will be based on various factors, such as skill, experience and qualification for the role.)

For roles open across multiple locations, the salary range indicated refers to the primary location. If a different location is considered, the applicable salary range will be communicated to candidates prior to the first interview.

What We Offer

We offer dynamic career opportunities across an international landscape. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to delivering value for all our employees and fostering a culture of respect.

Benefits

At CNH, we understand that the best solutions come from the diverse experiences and skills of our people. Here, you will be empowered to grow your career, to follow your passion, and help build a better future. To support our employees, we offer regional comprehensive benefits, including:

Flexible work arrangements

The Global Payment Tech team is the core engine powering ByteDance's global payment and financial services, spanning payment acquiring, wallets, financial products, insurance, and foreign exchange for users and merchants worldwide.

jobs.description:
Caltech is a world-renowned science and engineering institute that marshals some of the world's brightest minds and most innovative tools to address fundamental scientific questions. We thrive on finding and cultivating talented people who are passionate about what they do. Join us and be a part of the diverse Caltech community.

**Job Summary**

IPAC at Caltech has an opening for an Associate Applications Developer to participate in the development of the data processing pipelines for the UVEX mission.

IPAC, part of the Physics, Math, and Astronomy Division at Caltech (www.caltech.edu), provides science operations, user support, data and archive services, and scientific vision to maximize discovery with observatories both in space and on the ground.

The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) is targeted to launch in 2030 as NASA’s next Astrophysics Medium-Class Explorer mission. UVEX will undertake a synoptic survey of the entire sky in the near-UV and far-UV, probing the dynamic universe with a sensitivity more than 50 times better than GALEX. UVEX will also have a powerful broadband spectroscopic capability. UVEX will address fundamental questions from the Astro2020 Decadal Survey and study the evolution of low-metallicity, low-mass galaxies. UVEX time-domain surveys will probe the aftermaths of gravitational-wave-discovered compact object mergers, discover fast UV transients, and diagnose the early stages of explosive phenomena.

**Essential Job Duties**

As an Application Developer, you will work with the UVEX team to develop and test algorithms and write original production-quality code for pipeline processing and validation. You will also document your designs and software, and participate in meetings with the UVEX project.

**Basic Qualifications**

**If you have the following in your background, then we want to hear about your interest in joining our team:**

* Bachelor’s or equivalent degree in a technical subject such as Astronomy, Physics, Math, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Sciences, or a related field.
* 3+ years of experience as a software developer using Python and C/C++. In many cases, this can include experience obtained concurrent with your academic work.
* Familiarity with software configuration management principles and tools, source code version control (e.g., git/GitHub) and issue/bug tracking systems (e.g., Jira).

Beyond these basic qualifications, there are a set of skills and experiences which will add to your ability to contribute to the roles and responsibilities of an IPAC Applications Developer. The following might give you a head start here, but even if these do not describe you or your experience, we would still like to hear from you:

* Advanced degree in Astronomy, Physics, Math, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Sciences, or a related field.
* Experience working with scientific datasets and use cases.
* Experience developing software for astronomical data analysis.
* Experience with the Rubin/LSST Science Pipelines software stack.

* San Fernando, CA, United States

### **Company Description**

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at **Intuitive**. As a global leader in **robotic-assisted surgery** and **minimally invasive care**, our technologies—like the **da Vinci surgical system** and **Ion**—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help **transform the future of healthcare**, you’ll find your purpose here.

### **Job Description**

We’re looking for a Software Engineer who is passionate about building a modern, scalable Data as a Service (DaaS) platform that powers Intuitive’s Digital products and supports over 2,000 engineers across the organization. In this role, you will own and evolve critical components of our real-time and micro-batch data pipelines that power product development, internal tools, and analytics.

Your work will focus on enabling high-throughput, low-latency data delivery through streaming pipelines, dynamic transformations, and APIs, driving discoverability, accessibility, and actionable insights. You will help define the architecture and engineering practices that support self-service analytics and operational decision-making on scale.

As a catalyst for change, you will be at the forefront of reimagining how engineering teams consume and interact with data. Long-term success in this role means building robust, efficient systems and replacing legacy processes with modern solutions that allow teams to move faster, with greater confidence and autonomy.

Responsibilities:

* Design and build scalable, distributed Data as a Service that ingest, process, and serve data from robotics, manufacturing, engineering, and clinical sources in real time and batch modes.
* Develop and maintain robust APIs, data services, and tooling to provide internal teams with secure, efficient, and intuitive access to high-quality data.
* Partner with engineering, analytics, and business stakeholders to evolve data contracts and models that support emerging use cases and ensure semantic consistency.
* Implement CI/CD practices for data services, including automated testing for data quality, service reliability, and schema evolution.

jobs.title: Software Engineer — Reverse Engineering & Legacy Integrations
jobs.description:
About Psyrin

Psyrin builds AI for behavioral health. Our voice agent, Mira, runs the clinical interviews around a behavioral health visit: intake, consent, screening, and a structured psychiatric pre-assessment. It then drafts the assessment and treatment plan documentation for the clinician to review and sign.
Across our partner clinics, Mira has given clinicians 3.3× the assessment capacity per hour of manual assessment (as of September 2026). Psyrin is live with multiple behavioral health organizations, most of them community mental health and addiction providers, as well as work with state government. Our work serves Medicare and Medicaid patients, some of the most vulnerable populations in America.
The company was founded by doctors, psychologists, and AI researchers, largely from King's College London. We're published in Nature and backed by top thesis-driven investors.
While others build surface-level apps, we dig deep into the root causes of psychiatry's problems: inconsistent assessment quality, subjective diagnoses, and fragmented measurement systems. By capturing not just what patients say but how they say it, we're working toward our long-term vision: democratizing access to psychiatric evaluation and building precision psychiatry with AI. In short, an AI psychiatrist, built with the scientific rigor that mental healthcare demands.

The role

We're building an AI platform for mental healthcare, and we're looking for an exceptional engineer with experience reverse-engineering undocumented APIs and building connectors between legacy enterprise systems and modern applications.
We want someone who loves figuring out how complex software works from the outside, can reverse-engineer black-box behaviour, and turn their discoveries into reliable, production-grade integrations.

The challenge

We integrate with legacy Electronic Health Record (EHR) platforms, many built over 20 years ago on Oracle/PL-SQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and other legacy enterprise backends.
Behind these internal application APIs are complicated stored procedures, hidden server-side session state, inconsistent validation, and limited transactional guarantees.
We build Chrome browser extensions that use an authenticated user's session to interact with the same APIs used by the official EHR web application. A seemingly simple operation, such as creating a patient or saving a clinical note, can involve 10 or more dependent API calls.
The hardest part is not making the happy path work (although that isn't always easy). It's anticipating everything that could go wrong.
Without documentation or vendor support, you'll be responsible for proactively identifying and mitigating failure scenarios across long, stateful chains of operations: partial writes, unexpected server state, concurrency, duplicate records, interrupted requests, and subtle data-integrity issues. You'll need to reason about what the system might be doing internally, test your hypotheses, and design integrations that fail safely when assumptions don't hold.

What we're looking for

Real experience reverse-engineering software interfaces and building working integrations against undocumented APIs is our strongest requirement.
We're particularly interested in engineers who have built connectors into legacy systems by investigating how their existing applications communicate with their backends, rather than consuming officially supported, documented APIs.
Relevant experience might include:
Online travel booking:
Automating booking portals, travel-agent applications, or complex GDS workflows, particularly through reverse-engineered APIs, browser extensions, or browser-based automation.
Payroll and HR connectivity:
Building integrations into payroll providers or workforce platforms through undocumented web interfaces.
Insurance:
Automating legacy carrier portals, quoting systems, policy administration, or claims workflows.
Banking and financial connectivity:
Reverse-engineering online banking interfaces, account aggregation, or complex financial transaction workflows.
Other legacy enterprise software:
Building unsupported connectors, automation, or interoperability layers for complex, stateful applications.

The scale or commercial success of the project matters far less than what you personally figured out and built. Relevant experience could come from a substantial hobby project, an independent experiment, a one-person commercial product, or an engineering team.
You'll also need:
Strong JavaScript/TypeScript, HTTP, browser, and modern web application fundamentals.
Experience or strong familiarity with Chrome extensions, browser APIs, and session management.
Exceptional analytical reasoning, resourcefulness, and an ability to infer complex system behaviour from limited evidence.
Deep attention to correctness, concurrency, partial failures, and data integrity.
The ability to produce maintainable software while moving exceptionally quickly.
Proactivity and agency.
To be comfortable and happy with full ownership over integration.
Strong passion towards mental health and the company's mission.
Strategic planning around design and ability (or strong willingness) to anticipate diverse user behaviors.
Almost obsessive enthusiasm and interest in your field of work with the strong, continuous desire to improve.
To be comfortable with an early stage, high-velocity, quickly changing start up environment and work independently with minimal managerial oversight.
To have the ability to reflect, admit your mistakes, own them, learn from them and bounce back stronger.
To care - about your work, impact and colleagues.
Willingness to learn HIPAA requirements and handle protected health information carefully.
Able to travel to the US for business when needed.

How we work

We are a high-velocity engineering team. Our ambition is to build, in months, integrations that would traditionally take years to deliver in healthcare.
We're looking for someone who combines deep technical curiosity with urgency and execution. Someone equally comfortable with modern application architecture and the messy realities of legacy enterprise systems, who challenges assumptions, experiments rapidly, and finds creative ways around difficult technical constraints without compromising correctness.
We expect you to be highly proficient with modern AI-assisted engineering tools, using them to accelerate research, reverse engineering, implementation, testing, and iteration while independently validating their outputs.
We believe software engineering is changing fundamentally. We want someone who recognises that change, embraces emerging tools and techniques, and wants to help define what highly effective software engineering looks like over the next few years.
We care about exceptional ability, demonstrated ingenuity, agency and what you can actually build - not job titles, credentials, or years of experience.

Location and travel

Based in the San Francisco Bay Area or London. We'll also consider candidates elsewhere in the UK or US who can travel to San Francisco or London regularly.
We meet in person for a team retreat once a quarter.
You must already have the right to work in the UK or the US, and be able to travel to the US for business when needed.

Compensation and benefits

A competitive base salary, depending on experience and location.
An equity grant.
Benefits: unlimited PTO and quarterly in-person team retreats for everyone; in the US, 100% of premiums paid for PPO Platinum (or equivalent) health insurance plus dental and vision, a safe harbor 401(k) with a 3–5% employer match, one round-trip flight home a year, and Groundfloor membership for Bay Area staff; in the UK, a Revolut Ultra subscription and a NEST workplace pension. Full details on our careers page.
All work travel costs covered.

How to apply

Send your CV to careers@psyrin.ai with a short note on why you want to build in psychiatry and behavioral health, and how Psyrin's mission fits with yours.
Psyrin is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Embedded Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Proteus Space is a Los Angeles-based spacecraft technology company established to capitalize on a rapidly evolving space landscape and the urgent need to deliver resilient orbital capabilities to maintain and increase our national science and security interests. We combine serious space flight experience with an open minded, first-principles approach, leveraging advanced computational design and Industry 4.0 practices to deliver custom spacecraft and mission solutions with industry leading speed, precision, and reliability. We seek to enable every payload and mission with a fully custom, purpose-built spacecraft bus, designed and delivered using Proteus™, our patent-pending, automated computational design platform, with industry leading reliability.

**Role Description**

We are seeking an Embedded Flight Software Engineer with deep expertise in low-level embedded software, FPGA interfaces, drivers, and bootloader development to join our flight program team. This is a full-time, in-office role for an experienced professional with a proven track record of hands-on FSW development. In this role, you will design and implement low-level drivers, BSPs, and boot systems while managing memory architectures and FPGA hardware interfaces. You will bridge the gap between low-level hardware and high-level FSW logic, ensuring reliable spacecraft boot behavior, fail-safe recovery, and deterministic bus communications in space environments.

**Key Responsibilities**.

* Develop low-level C/C++ drivers, Board Support Packages (BSPs), and hardware interfaces for microcontrollers, FPGAs, and standard communication buses.
* Design and implement stage-1 and stage-2 bootloaders, robust boot behaviors, partition swapping logic, and fail-safe recovery modes.
* Architect memory management strategies across volatile and non-volatile memory (NOR/NAND Flash, SRAM, EEPROM) to preserve data integrity across reboots.
* Configure low-level communication protocols and bus interfaces (e.g., SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, SpaceWire, or PCIe) between compute units, peripherals, and payloads.
* Implement telemetry collection, time synchronization, and task scheduling within RTOS or embedded OS environments.
* Execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and debugging on flatsats using logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and FPGA emulator tools.
* Manage the codebase using modern version control systems and contribute to CI/CD workflows for automated testing and continuous integration.
* Execute comprehensive test campaigns on testbeds and flight units to verify software performance under flight-like conditions.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate subsystems with the spacecraft main compute element.
* Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.
* Document design processes, test results, and system performance.
* Provide technical guidance on FSW architectures to fellow engineers, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or advanced degree in computer science, aerospace engineering, or similar field.
* 5+ years of embedded software engineering experience, with exposure to low-level driver development, hardware integration, or bootloaders.
* Strong proficiency in C, C++, embedded Linux, and Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS).
* Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and automated testing/CI workflows.
* Strong ability to collaborate effectively in a dynamic environment while maintaining a positive and professional attitude.
* Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
* Must possess or be willing and eligible to obtain a United States Department of Defense Top Secret security clearance.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Experience writing custom drivers for FPGA logic blocks or hardware interfaces (such as I2C, CAN, SPI, UART, or SpaceWire).
* Experience with hardware-level communication protocols and hardware/software integration.
* Experience working in clean room environments and adhering to ESD protocols.
* Demonstrated experience with custom bootloader design, memory controller drivers, Flash file systems, and image verification/recovery techniques.

**Salary Range:** $130,000 - $180,000 per year. Final compensation is based on experience, education and qualifications.

**Benefits**

Proteus Space offers comprehensive benefits including paid medical healthcare for employees, flexible vacation policy, sick days, 401k matching option, pregnancy leave, family leave, holiday pay, military service leave, dental care, vision care and other benefits.

**Equal Opportunity**

Proteus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities regardless of an applicant's age, disability, sex, race, religion, gender, national origin, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. The Company will provide reasonable accommodations to an applicant with a disability or religious belief in or to enable the applicant to apply for the position.

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm is building the next generation of customer identity and authentication. This role is a hands-on, mid-engineering position inside Information Security, contributing to core CIAM capabilities that protect customers and support growth.

You will help build and maintain backend services that power registration, login, authorization, and account lifecycle flows across B2C and B2B experiences. You will work with experienced engineers and partner teams to deliver scoped identity features with strong security fundamentals, reliability, and operational rigor.

### **What you'll do**

* Build and ship customer-facing authentication features—from smoother login experiences to MFA, step-up authentication, and device binding—with mentorship from experienced engineers.
* Develop backend services and APIs in Python or Kotlin, turning product requirements into working software that helps customers access their accounts securely.
* Work with modern identity technologies such as Okta, Auth0, and ForgeRock, writing custom code and integrations that connect identity capabilities to web, mobile, and partner applications.
* Take scoped features through the software development lifecycle: contribute to design, write readable code and automated tests, participate in code reviews, and deploy to production with support from the team.
* Solve real engineering problems by debugging services, improving reliability, and using logs and metrics to understand how your code behaves in production.
* Collaborate with engineering and product partners, learn secure development practices, and grow your software engineering skills while building expertise in authentication.

  

### **What we look for**

We're looking for a Mid-Level Software Engineer with solid engineering fundamentals, a passion for authentication, and an eagerness to learn customer identity and access management. You do not need extensive authentication or CIAM experience—we value your ability to build software, solve problems, and grow in the space.

* Demonstrated ability to write, test, and debug software in Python, Kotlin, or a similar language through coursework, internships, personal projects, open source, or professional work. No fixed minimum years of experience required.

Candidates who join KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business before the spin-off will transition to Trinzic when the separation is complete and will not need to reapply for employment. 

Job Summary

KBR is seeking an NS4R Software Developer to join our team in Colorado Springs, CO or El Segundo, CA.

This job supports SSC within the Joint Terminal Engineering Office (JTEO) as a developer on the National Security SATCOM Systems Synchronization Roadmap (NS4R) software application. The NS4R application is hosted on Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) MilCloud and requires close coordination with DISA to resolve issues in a timely manner. In support of JTEO, duties include maintaining the NS4R database including security upgrades, development and implementation of enhancements to the NS4R tool, providing user held desk support, maintaining user accounts, providing NS4R database backups, maintaining configuration control and backups of the source code, support JTEO to evaluate and address security requirements and perform troubleshooting. As needed, you can expect to train Government and FFRDC personnel on the use and maintenance of the NS4R tool and database.

jobs.description:
Overview

Job Description:

We don’t simply hire employees. We invest in them. When you work at Chatham, we empower you — offering professional development opportunities to help you grow in your career, no matter if you've been here for five months or 15 years. Chatham has worked hard to create a distinct work environment that values people, teamwork, integrity, and client service. You will have immediate opportunities to partner with talented subject matter experts, work on complex projects, and contribute to the value Chatham delivers every day.

Chatham Financials' Summer Internship Program offers a dynamic and immersive experience for aspiring technology professionals. This is your opportunity to gain hands-on software engineering experience in a leading finance and technology firm while contributing to projects that drive our business forward.

As a Software Engineering Intern at Chatham, you will be immersed in a collaborative team environment where you'll work alongside experienced engineers on cutting-edge products. Whether you're developing new features, optimizing systems, or solving complex problems, you'll play a key role in shaping the future of finance through technology.

Our technology team is made up of a team of Software Engineers, Testers, DevOps Engineers, Security Engineers, UX Designers, Quantitative Analysts and Data Base Analysts. We build software for our clients that range across multiple sectors and industries as well as tools for our internal users to help them better serve our clients. Our team is a global team located in four different countries and multiple time zones. We interact daily with each other as well as our key business stakeholders to ensure quality and speedy delivery of our product offerings.  

What You’ll Do

"Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham"
Assist with developing cutting-edge financial applications; develop innovative, high-quality, and robust web applications and micro services as part of our growing application development team. 
Be a member of an agile scrum team that owns development of a specific product or platform. 
Collaborate with other software engineering teams, design team, quant team, product owners and managers, and business stakeholders, while working on intern project. 
Develop software in our technology stack which is constantly evolving but currently includes .NET,  ASP.NET, React, Angular, TypeScript, SQL Server, RabbitMQ and Redis. 
Build automated unit, integration and front-end tests using xUnit, Moq, NSubstitute and Cypress among other technologies. 
Implement the build, test, deploy development cycle in CI/CD pipelines using Docker, YAML, Gitlab CI, and Hashicorp Nomad
Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham

What You’ll Need: 

Working towards Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. 
2 years of experience preferred
Experience with object-oriented languages such as C#, C++ or Java 
Experience with JavaScript and JavaScript frameworks (e.g. React) 
Experience with relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle or MySQL 
Understanding of Unit testing, Test-Driven Development and mocking frameworks 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Understanding of REST principles, Service-oriented architecture, and API development 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Proclivity towards refactoring and continuously improving OO code through agile development methods. 
Open-source development projects. 
Contributions to the local developer community. 
Quantitative and modeling skills with an ability to learn techniques in numerical optimization, data mining, simulation, or model calibration. 

This role offers flexibility and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement.

Chatham Financial offers an entrepreneurial culture that rewards teamwork and innovation. We seek individuals who are natural leaders, quick learners, and fit our collaborative culture. Join us to develop your fullest potential, impact our clients and community, and kickstart your career in finance.

Apply now and become a part of Chatham Financial's legacy of excellence and innovation!

Applicants must be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate academic program at the junior or senior level.

The internship program will begin on June 1, 2027, and runs through August 6, 2027. Applicants must be available for the duration of the program, Monday – Friday from 8:30am-5:30pm, onsite in your designated office.

Chatham Financial is the leading independent capital markets advisor, delivering an integrated blend of expert advice and powerful technology to help you reduce risk and seize opportunity. With decades of capital markets strategy, execution, monitoring, and performance expertise, we serve as an unwavering advocate for your best interests and your innovation partner. Our technology platform unifies data across assets, debt, and derivatives, giving you unmatched agility, transparency, and insight.

It’s clear ahead.

Our commitment is to carry that light forward in every partnership, every solution, and every market we serve.

We help guide the way—giving clients the insight and momentum to move forward with confidence, no matter what lies ahead.

jobs.title: UI/UX Software Engineer - NREC
jobs.description:
At the National Robotics Engineering Center (NREC), it is our engineers and technicians who drive the breakthroughs that define our success. The members of our technical staff collaborate closely with leadership and multidisciplinary teams to design, build, and deploy sophisticated robotic solutions that address complex challenges in industrial, commercial and government sectors. Each project benefits from their expertise, creativity, and hands-on problem-solving, fueling progress and innovation across the organization.

As part of our dedicated team, you will work alongside world-class robotics professionals committed to pushing the boundaries of technology and redefining ideas into solutions for real-world applications. We foster a culture of professionalism, respect, and collaboration, offering a flexible and encouraging environment where you can sharpen your skills, lead impactful projects, and take control of your career development.

We are seeking a dynamic UI/UX Software Engineer for existing and new projects. In this position, you will work on a variety of user interfaces for robotic systems. You will have an opportunity to collaborate on an internal team and with sponsoring partners to support the work through all lifecycle stages. Our team has members with diverse backgrounds both in robotics and other industries aligned to make robust software and firmware that is useful in the world. Projects you may support range from industrial machine operator assist systems to agricultural productivity tools and beyond to other automation, autonomy, or safety systems. Your day-to-day work will include developing user interfaces for internal and external usage centered around robotic systems.

Your Primary Responsibilities Include

Co-Design Human-Machine Interfaces: Partner closely with robotics engineers, hardware teams, and field operators to design custom, intuitive interfaces for complex robotic systems.
Build Native Qt/QML Frontends: Develop fluid, hardware-accelerated user interfaces using QML and/or Qt, binding them smoothly to backend C++ or Python data streams.
Prototype & Test with Real Users: Prototype interaction flows and collaborate directly with end-users to evaluate usability, safety, and operator performance in the field.
Integrate Real-Time System Data: Connect UI components to central system state engines, telemetry feeds, and databases while ensuring the interface remains fast and responsive.
Champion Collaborative Software Development: Actively participate in an inclusive team culture through constructive peer reviews of both designs and code, integration testing, version control, and clear documentation.
Integrate & Adapt APIs: Adapt open-source libraries, proprietary tools, and backend APIs to extend UI capabilities cleanly and maintainably.
Cross-Functional Field Testing: Validate and refine interfaces through hands-on testing with both simulated environments and physical robotic hardware alongside the broader engineering team.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience: B.S. in Computer Science, HCI, Design, or equivalent practical experience, with 1–3+ years of combined academic or professional software development experience.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Integration and Test
jobs.description:
Company Overview
At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.
Position Overview
We are seeking a Software Engineer to own the software that provisions, calibrates, and tests our robots, from the manufacturing line through service and repair. Your goal: every robot that leaves the line or comes back from repair works as a complete system, and technicians can verify it without engineering help. You will own escalations from manufacturing and service: you triage, dig in, fix what's yours, and drive cross-team resolution when it's not. Your work means engineers and researchers can trust the robots they use, so model evaluations reflect the model, not a faulty robot.
This is a hands-on role at the point where hardware, firmware, and software come together. Alongside building test software, you will turn recurring failures into lasting product and process improvements. You will work closely with manufacturing, hardware, firmware, perception, and robotics teams, as well as the technicians who build and repair our robots.
Responsibilities
Build automated manufacturing tests that verify each robot is fully functional before it leaves the line, with results tracked for each robot.
Turn engineering scripts for provisioning, flashing, and calibration, such as camera calibration, into guided workflows technicians can run.
Build one-click service tests that let technicians verify a robot is fully repaired before handing it back.
Build startup self-checks that verify each robot's hardware, software versions, and configuration every time it boots.
Define pass/fail criteria with the hardware, perception, and controls teams that own each subsystem.
Root-cause test failures across hardware, firmware, and software, and drive fixes with the owning teams.
Track failure modes and repeat issues, and feed learnings back into design, assembly, and test processes.

Preferred Qualifications
BS, MS or higher degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum of 3 years of industry experience.
Proficiency in Python and C++.
Experience writing software that interfaces with real hardware, such as motors, sensors, and embedded devices.
Experience building automated tests, manufacturing test stations, or technician-facing test tools.
Comfort debugging across hardware and software, including reading schematics and working with communication buses like CAN or EtherCAT.
Experience with Linux and ROS/ROS2 or similar robotics middleware.
Familiarity with camera calibration or sensor bring-up is a plus.

You'll help build the systems that let us protect privacy and make definitive statements about our practices from data inventory and classification through access and purpose controls to retention, deletion, and audit. You'll also collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to answer privacy questions that don’t have textbook answers.

This is a role for someone who knows privacy deeply and treats it as an engineering problem rather than a checklist. The questions we face are rarely settled by policy alone: what it means to honor a deletion request against a trained model; how customers' fine-tuning data on Tinker should be isolated, never commingled, and only used for the customer; when to deidentify data (and how) vs. apply differential privacy to it. We want someone who can weigh privacy against model quality, research velocity, and product usefulness, pick a defensible answer, and then build it.

What You'll Do

Implement and enforce privacy and data governance across internal systems day to day by building systems like data classification tagging, retention jobs, deletion pipelines, and data classifiers and integrating them across systems at Thinking Machines.
Build the isolation guarantees that keep customer and user data separate and protected, including the training data customers bring to Tinker and the conversations people have with our interfaces.
Run privacy reviews and threat models on new data sources, training runs, and product features, and close them out by shipping the control, the check, or the tooling, not only a recommendation.
Translate legal and policy requirements (GDPR, CCPA, contractual commitments) into working code: policy-as-code, CI checks, and pipeline enforcement, built and maintained by you.
Maintain shared libraries and guardrails that make the private path the default, and fix them when they break or fall out of date.

Skills and Qualifications

Minimum qualifications
Built and shipped at least one production privacy or data governance system (retention/deletion pipeline, policy evaluation engine, data cataloging and/or lineage system, consent system, or similar) and owned it through to operation, not just design.
Written and operated production code in Python or a comparable language, evidenced by a system you can walk through in detail: what it does, how it fails, how you debugged it.
Direct experience with enforcing privacy or governing data in an AI/ML data pipeline (training data, fine-tuning, inference, or evaluation) and can describe a specific privacy risk you identified or mitigated in one of these systems.
Has chosen pragmatic controls over ideal ones on real systems, and can describe what was shipped as a result.
Has written a technical requirement or control directly from a legal or policy obligation (GDPR, CCPA, or similar), and can name the obligation and the control.

Preferred qualifications
Experience at an AI lab or with ML infrastructure: training data curation, multi-tenant fine-tuning platforms, or inference systems that handle user data.
Has implemented a privacy-enhancing technique (deidentification, differential privacy, secure enclaves) in a real system, and can describe where it fell short.
Experience building data lineage, metadata, or policy-engine tooling, or large-scale deletion and retention systems.
Background in security engineering, or has worked directly with a security team on access control implementation.
Has been one of the first engineers building out a privacy function, and can point to the specific systems they personally built, not just the program they ran.

Logistics

Location: This role is based in San Francisco, California.
Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $300,000 - $350,000 USD.
Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can't guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you're the right fit, we're committed to working through the visa process together.
Benefits: Thinking Machines offers generous health, dental, and vision benefits, unlimited PTO, paid parental leave, and relocation support as needed.

To tie features like these together, we are building a general Game Server Management product to unify developers' observability and control of their servers.

At its core, this team is focused on solving complex back end distributed systems and networking problems at scale. However, our scope extends to full stack projects spanning all the way from the infrastructure layer, through engine development, data pipelines, microservices, telemetry, game servers, web development, UI, and UX design. This team collaborates on multiple cross-company efforts and our projects are of extremely high importance to Roblox.
