Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and at milk processing and PRMP plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, collect samples for regulatory surveillance, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairy farms, milk processing plants, bulk milk haulers and other dairy food and PRMP facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard dairy products to California consumers.

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. Most of the workday will be spent traveling in a state vehicle to various locations throughout the region.

  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperature, fumes and gases. The noise level in equipment rooms may be high. The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch (MDFS) is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMPs) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. Research Data Analyst 1 (5272C), Environmental Science, Policy, and Management #89414 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is home to multidisciplinary research programs that recognize the urgency of the challenges-and the enormous opportunities-that may lead to transformative change. We have award-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach who are all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Coastal Climate Resilience Lab (PI Rachel Carlson) seeks a Research Data Analyst 1 in the area of remote sensing and geospatial analysis. This is a part-time position (20 hours per week).
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 will conduct data analysis supporting two ongoing research collaborations:
  
  
Remote sensing of freshwater plumes in California (PI Carlson and co-PIs Albert Ruhi and Kelly Hondula)
  
Effects of land use and land cover on nearshore marine environments (PI Carlson).
  
  
This position involves preparing and analyzing ecological datasets using established remote sensing and geospatial methods under the direct supervision of other researchers. The Research Data Analyst 1 will apply data science and quantitative modeling methods to map freshwater flux in the marine environment and evaluate interlocking patterns in human-dominated landscapes and benthic ecosystems. This position works in a team to coordinate data cleaning, quality control, and code documentation, complete computational analysis, and prepare data visualizations displaying analytical results for internal review.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would be based in the research laboratory of PI Dr. Rachel Carlson on the UC Berkeley campus. They would also be co-mentored by Dr. Albert Ruhi (co-PI, ESPM, Berkeley) and remotely by Dr. Kelly Hondula (Arizona State University). They would receive additional guidance from at least one PhD student. Remote working arrangements are considered.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would have the opportunity to participate in campus data science, wilderness first aid, and other professional development opportunities. They would have the opportunity to attend one USA-based conference each year. The PI's group provides a supportive work environment that recognizes and supports people of diverse identities and needs and prioritizes inclusive practices and field safety.

Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.

Create reports and basic visualizations on results.
  
  
15%
  
  
Supports testing of research instruments and data sources.

10%
  
  
Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.
  
  
10%
  
  
Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.
  
  
5%
  
  
Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with evaluation and research of data reporting products.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  
Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  
Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  
Basic consultation and communication skills.
  
  
Education / Training
  
  
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing  
services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist II
jobs.description:
About FACS

At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.
Our Values

We live our mission through three core values:
People First:
Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
Integrity of the Science:
Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence-based practices.
Client Relationships for Life:
Build long-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

Why Join Us

At FACS, you’ll contribute meaningful work that helps organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. You’ll join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven team that values scientific integrity, strong client relationships, and professional growth.
Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications, so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.
Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at FACS Experts.
About the Role

The Environmental Health Specialist II is a hands-on, field-based role supporting industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial (mold and moisture) projects. The Specialist performs on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, air sampling, clearances, and project monitoring, and prepares clear, accurate written field reports.
This role may take the lead on assigned projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned, coordinating closely with the Project Manager, contractors, and clients. Local travel to client and project sites is a regular part of the role.
Fieldwork and Reporting

Perform on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, and monitoring for industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial projects.
Perform asbestos air sampling, clearances, and on-site analysis of air samples while adhering to quality-control requirements.
Prepare written field reports and maintain acceptable report turnaround times.
Identify and secure necessary tools and equipment for assigned projects.
Maintain internal QA/QC compliance.

Project Coordination and Communication

Take the lead on projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned.
Communicate vital project information to Project Managers to support coordination and progress tracking.
Serve as a liaison between the client, Project Manager, and contractor.
Report project progress and provide technical input to the Project Manager.
Obtain and track project numbers for accurate record-keeping.
Adapt the scope of work in the field as needed to accommodate actual conditions or changes during project progression.

Compliance and Contractor Oversight

Review contractor personnel certifications, medical clearances, and other required documentation to ensure compliance with abatement requirements.
Act as a point of contact and meet with regulatory agents in the event of surprise site inspections.

Team Development and Professional Growth

Assist with training and mentoring junior staff.
Attend required internal and external technical training.
Maintain technical certifications.

Experience

Minimum of two years of experience as a field technician conducting field surveys, inspections, assessments, or asbestos-related monitoring work.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, and ability to quickly learn new software and systems.

Education and Credentials

Bachelor of Science in industrial hygiene, health and safety, biological science, physical science, or a related field—or equivalent relevant experience.
Current California Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) certification required.

Preferred Experience

Experience with asbestos abatement monitoring, air sampling, clearances, or indoor environmental quality work.
Experience serving as a field lead or coordinating with contractors, clients, or junior staff.

Physical & Work Requirements

Physical ability to stoop, kneel, climb, crawl, walk, and stand for extended periods in varied work environments while performing sampling activities
Ability to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for documentation and reporting
Must be able to pass a background check, annual medical examinations, and OSHA-required respirator fit tests
Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
Ability to travel locally to assigned client and project sites

Compensation and Rewards

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus structure tied to individual and team achievements
Comprehensive benefits package, including:
Medical coverage with 100% company-paid premiums for employees and their families, plus 50% of the annual deductible covered by the company
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions
Vision and dental plan options
Flexible Spending Accounts (health care and dependent care)
Company-sponsored programs including Employee Assistance Program, life and disability insurance, Rocket Lawyer legal services, and mobile phone plan with Verizon
Voluntary benefits options including supplemental life insurance for employees and dependents, short-term disability, hospital, accident, and pet insurance
Generous PTO (3 weeks accrual), paid holidays, volunteer days, and floating holiday
Tuition Reimbursement Program to promote higher education
Paid training and certifications to support career advancement
Incentive Bonus Plan and Donation Matching Program

Wage Transparency

Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.

If you are a certified CSST or experienced environmental health field professional who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, asbestos and microbial projects, and supporting clients and project teams, we encourage you to apply. We welcome all candidates to apply, including women, people of color, persons with disabilities, and veterans.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist III / Senior Environmental Scientist
to join our Environmental Remediation Practice in Richmond, California
.

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership and project coordination for environmental investigation, remediation, groundwater monitoring, compliance, and emergency response projects throughout Northern California and the western United States. This position will support a diverse portfolio of industrial, energy, transportation, municipal, and commercial clients while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams of scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience managing environmental field programs, coordinating subcontractors and laboratories, overseeing health and safety compliance, managing environmental data, and preparing technical and regulatory deliverables.

This position will be based in Richmond, California, with opportunities to support projects throughout Northern California and the western United States.

Responsibilities

Technical and Project Leadership

Lead environmental investigation, monitoring, remediation, and compliance projects from planning through execution.
Coordinate field schedules, staffing, subcontractors, laboratory services, equipment, and site logistics.
Develop and implement work plans, sampling plans, health and safety documentation, and project-specific field procedures.
Support project managers with project planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource forecasting, and client communications.
Identify project risks and develop solutions to achieve project objectives while maintaining quality, schedule, and budget commitments.

Groundwater Monitoring and Remediation

Plan and oversee groundwater, soil, sediment, and waste characterization programs.
Manage groundwater monitoring events and environmental sampling activities.
Coordinate remedial investigations, corrective action programs, groundwater treatment systems, and in-situ remediation efforts.
Evaluate environmental data and support development of remedial strategies and technical recommendations.
Ensure field activities are performed in accordance with project requirements and applicable regulations.

Environmental Compliance

Support environmental compliance programs for industrial, infrastructure, remediation, and construction projects.
Conduct environmental inspections, audits, and compliance assessments.
Monitor project activities for compliance with permits, mitigation measures, Environmental Protection Plans (EPPs), and Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs).
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, contractors, and stakeholders to support permitting and environmental compliance objectives.

Health and Safety

Implement and enforce site-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs), Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), and company safety procedures.
Lead daily safety meetings, hazard assessments, and pre-task planning activities.
Support atmospheric monitoring, radiological monitoring, confined-space activities, and other specialized health and safety requirements.
Promote a strong safety culture through leadership, mentoring, and continuous improvement.

Technical Reporting and Data Management

Prepare and review technical reports, groundwater monitoring reports, regulatory submittals, and field documentation.
Perform QA/QC reviews of environmental data, field records, and project deliverables.
Manage environmental databases and electronic reporting platforms, including EQuIS and GeoTracker.
Support data validation, interpretation, and presentation of technical findings to clients and regulatory agencies.

Team Development

Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior environmental professionals.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, geologists, engineers, biologists, technicians, and subcontractors.
Support staff development through field training, technical mentoring, and knowledge sharing initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related field and 4+ years environmental consulting or related professional experience (groundwater monitoring, environmental sampling, remediation field activities, and environmental compliance programs, leading project teams, coordinating complex environmental projects, experience preparing technical reports and regulatory deliverables, etc.) or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Employment is contingent upon successfully completing a pre-employment background check and drug screen.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting California environmental remediation programs, including DTSC, RWQCB, and GeoTracker reporting requirements.
Experience at refinery, chemical, manufacturing, terminal, energy, or other industrial facilities, including CERCLA, RCRA, corrective action, and groundwater remediation programs.
Experience managing subcontractors, coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, and supporting emergency response and disaster recovery.
Experience with complex groundwater monitoring and reporting, environmental site investigations, remediation, compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Proficiency in EQuIS, GeoTracker, environmental database management, QA/QC, data validation, technical report preparation, SWPPP compliance, HASPs, JSAs, atmospheric and radiological monitoring.
Relevant training and certifications: current OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER, OSHA 8-Hour HAZWOPER Refresher, OSHA Site Supervisor Training, RCRA Hazardous Waste Management Training, Radiation Safety or Radiological Monitoring Training, Confined Space Entry Training, and First Aid/CPR Certification.

Revolution Medicines is a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on developing novel targeted therapies to inhibit frontier targets in RAS-addicted cancers. The company’s R&D pipeline comprises RAS(ON) Inhibitors designed to suppress diverse oncogenic variants of RAS proteins, and RAS Companion Inhibitors for use in combination treatment strategies. As a new member of the Revolution Medicines team, you will join other outstanding scientists in a tireless commitment to patients with cancers harboring mutations in the RAS signaling pathway.

The Opportunity:

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Research Associate to support laboratory research activities focused on the development and execution of investigative toxicology (iTox) predictive assays and workflows to enable improved safety translation to the clinic. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of the technical needs in a lab as well as significant hands-on experience with standard/bespoke cell culture and in vitro cell biology techniques. Further, the successful candidate will:

Develop novel approach methods (NAMs) including predictive 2D/3D models for nonclinical safety assessments.
Independently perform experiments related to in vitro/ex vivo 2D/3D assays using lab techniques that include cell viability/cell death, flow cytometry, primary cell culture, animal sample processing, molecular and cell isolation, immunofluorescence, plate-based reporter assays and ELISA/Luminex
Support in vivo study design, data analysis, study coordination and sample management
Analyze, interpret and accurately document assay/study results in an electronic lab notebook or other technical reporting formats
Work independently and collaboratively in a team to ensure timely and accurate data analysis and communication to support decision-making and contribute to high-quality study reports.
Support the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of lab instruments and contribute to the evaluation and adoption of new technologies for enhanced toxicity prediction, compound screening, and development of translational safety biomarkers.
Manage day-to-day experimental/study related activities in the lab and work effectively with Contract Research Organizations (CROs), RevMed study operations, internal scientists and subject matter experts (SMEs).
Maintain a safe and organized lab environment and support development and/or review of protocols, SOPs, policies, and guidelines.

Required Skills, Experience, and Education:

Bachelor/Master’s degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences or a related scientific discipline, with 5+ of relevant industry experience or 3+ years of postgraduate working experience.
Hands-on experience in operating and maintaining cell culture and standard lab instruments.
Experience maintaining lab environment, lab infrastructure and sample management.
Experience with animal sample processing and advanced cell culture techniques for immortalized cell lines, primary cells (including PBMCs) and/or iPSC cells.
Cell and molecular biology methods, including flow cytometry, Luminex/MSD, ELISA, cell viability/death assays.
Ability to conduct multiple laboratory and project tasks efficiently.
Ability to work in a team-oriented environment with flexibility.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, excellent record-keeping skills, and being able to adapt to a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.

Preferred Skills:

Experience working with small molecules and targeted oncology therapeutics of all modalities.
Experience working in a matrixed team environment at a biotech/pharma company or CRO.
3D assays, data analytics/ in silico experience is a plus.

* Conducting field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks.

Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our Pacific Northwest and National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Engineering, or closely related field (i.e., environmental, biological, physical science)

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Science degree in Geology, Engineering or closely related field (i.e., environmental, biological, physical science)
* Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $55,200- $82,800. jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
APTIM is seeking a motivated entry-level Environmental Scientist to support our portfolio of federal environmental investigation and remediation projects. Projects commonly involve the investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by chlorinated solvents, petroleum, radiological contaminants, or emerging compounds. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of project managers and partner with other engineers, scientists, geologists, risk assessors, and health physicists.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Assist with the collection, documentation, and organization of field data to support project objectives.
* Contribute to the preparation of project work plans and deliverables.
* Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimates for proposal efforts.
* Develop and maintain spreadsheets, dashboards, and data-tracking tools.
* Assist in the management, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical analysis and data visualization tools.
* Identify and evaluate environmental risks and recommend remediation strategies to support compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Adhere to established health and safety policies and procedures and execute work in a safe and conscientious manner.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science or a related scientific discipline (completed or in progress).
* Relevant internship, research, or academic project experience involving environmental investigation, water or wastewater treatment, sustainability, or ecological conservation (0–2 years).
* Strong interest in environmental remediation, field investigations, treatment systems, and environmental compliance.
* Must have strong written and oral communication skills.
* Willingness to learn field sampling methods, equipment operation, and environmental data collection procedures.
* Ability to perform essential field duties, including walking on uneven terrain, lifting and carrying field equipment, and working outdoors in varying weather conditions.
* Ability to wear and use required PPE.
* Ability to travel to work sites, including overnight travel.
* Valid driver's license.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or authorized to work on federal contracts.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Completion of 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training.
* Experience using AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or similar tools) to support technical communication, analytical tasks, research, and efficient project execution. Upon hire, employees are expected to use these tools in accordance with approved company guidelines.

**About APTIM**

APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

What you can expect from APTIM:

* Work that is worthy of your time and talent
* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
* A voice in making our company better
* Investment into your personal and professional development

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $33.00 to $40.00 per hour Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.

**Employee Benefits**

APTIM Federal Services, llc is committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.

* Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and several carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.
* Company paid and optional Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance
* Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity coverage
* Paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave (eligibility based on company policy and applicable law)
* 401(k) APTIM offers three 401k plans through the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (PEP). The specific plan you are eligible for depends on the business unit you are in. The details of the largest plan are found here:

* + APTIM 401(k) Guide
  + APTIM - Helpful Documents

**About APTIM - In Pursuit of Better**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking to be a part of a dynamic team of conservation-minded scientists working to protect fish and wildlife resources in the redwood and Douglas fir forests, oak woodlands, chaparral, and grasslands of the San Francisco Bay Area? The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Wildfire Resiliency Program is seeking a motivated professional to work as a Senior Environmental Scientist Specialist reviewing and evaluating vegetation management and fuel reduction projects, and Timber Emergencies and Exemptions by analyzing consequences of proposed activities, attending site visits and inspections, preparing written reports and recommendations for the conservation of fish and wildlife resources, assessing the application of law, regulation and policy, conducting listed and sensitive species consultations, and preparing any related Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements and Incidental Take Permits.

The incumbent works in close collaboration with other Environmental Scientists and Senior Environmental Scientists, and with other state agencies. Under the direction of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) the incumbent represents the region and acts as the staff lead and provides consultative advice when working with applicants, local, state and federal agencies, stakeholders, and the general public. Public contacts made in the course of this work are sensitive and involve a wide variety of special interest groups.

Performance of specified activities will require an in-depth knowledge of administrative procedures, Department policies, applicable environmental laws and regulations, and ecological principles to protect fish and wildlife resources. Strong written and oral communication skills are necessary. Problem-solving, organizational skills and a positive attitude towards teamwork are essential. Fieldwork in rugged terrain is required.

**Company Description**

*“I've been with AECOM for over a decade, and when I reflect on why I stay with the company it is because of workplace culture and the nature of our projects. Working on impactful community-shaping projects with unique and diverse challenges, having opportunities for meaningful career progression, and being a part of a caring, close-knit team that supports each other through life's ups and downs.” –* ***Alix Chinnery, Associate Director - Environment, Perth, WA***

**Come grow with us.**

AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.

**Everyone belongs at AECOM.**

We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging - because great ideas come from diverse perspectives. AECOM is proud to be a **Fortune 500 Most Admired Company**, a **WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality**, #**Work180 Equitable Workplace Awards 2025 Winner** and an **AWEI Bronze Tier LGBTQ+ Inclusive Employer**.

 **Job Description**

We are looking for a passionate Graduate Environmental Planner / Scientist to join our **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)** teamin Newcastle.

At AECOM, our Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) team is helping deliver some of the most transformational projects in Australia – from renewable energy and transmission projects, to major road, rail, water and industrial developments. We combine innovative technologies with decades of expertise to deliver robust, easy-to-understand analyses that achieve compliance, support clients’ Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) objectives, and create meaningful change for communities.

**How you'll make a difference:**

* Apply your environmental science, planning, or engineering qualifications to real-world challenges.
* Work with multi-disciplinary teams of scientists, planners, engineers, drafters, project administrators and contractors in a fast-paced consulting environment.
* Develop skills in environmental assessment across renewable energy, water, and transport sectors, as well as in navigating approval pathways under Commonwealth, State, and local frameworks.
* Support ESG initiatives by engaging with communities and key stakeholders.
* Embed sustainability and resilience outcomes within projects.

You’ll have opportunities to collaborate across Australia, New Zealand and globally, with access to a strong pipeline of projects and a network of mentors to help you shape your career.

**What our Graduate Program offers:**

* **Graduate Introduction:** Kickstart connections with peers and leaders.
* **Essential Consulting Skills:** Master core consulting skills from day one.
* **Networking and Learning:** Grow your network and industry know-how.
* **Mentoring and Career Support:** Receive guidance from experienced professionals.
* **Learning from Experts:** Learn directly from industry leaders and specialists.
* **Flexible Work Options:** Work in a way that fits your life and wellbeing.
* **Career Pathways:** Get support to progress and step confidently into your next role.

For more information, visit our Early Careers website.

 **Qualifications**  

* **Graduate Attributes:** We’re seeking graduates with strong communication and teamwork skills, a proactive and adaptable mindset, and a commitment to professionalism and integrity.
* **Bachelor’s Degree:** You must be in your final year or completed a Bachelor’s or Postgraduate degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Planning, Environmental Engineering.
* **Graduate Year:** You must have completed your studies and have graduated before starting the program.
* **Commencement:** You must be able to commence work by February 2027. We are open to mid-year finishers who are able to commence by July 2027.
* **Working Rights:** You must have full working rights to work in Australia before applying. We do accept candidates with student and graduate visas.

  
**Additional Information**

**Our Recruitment Process**

* **Submit Your Application:** Complete the job application, uploading your resume, cover letter and the latest copy of your academic transcripts as one single document.
* **Interview:** Attend a face-to-face interview at your local office.

*Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.*

**What sets us apart?**

We are the trusted global infrastructure leader.

Across the globe, we partner with our clients in the public and private sectors to solve their most complex challenges, pioneer innovative solutions and deliver a better world.

Our reputation is recognised globally. We are named the world’s top design firm and ranked #1 in Transportation, General Building, and Environmental Engineering by Engineering News-Record in 2025.

We are also honoured to be listed among Fortune’s “World’s Most Admired Companies” for the twelfth consecutive year and recognised as one of the 2025 World’s Most Ethical Companies by Ethisphere for our commitment to integrity and creating positive impact.

**Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?**

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

jobs.title: Associate Consultant, Air Quality
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

**Inviting bright minds**

Do you want to develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and creative culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world.  
  
Ramboll is seeking an Air Quality Intern to join the firm’s offices in Los Angeles or Irvine, California, or Phoenix, Arizona in Spring/Summer 2027. If you are detail-oriented, self-motivated and enjoy thinking “outside-of-the-box,” please apply! If you can work in a team, apply analytical skills, and are looking to get your hands dirty (literally and figuratively), then you may find Ramboll to be an ideal place to start your career.

 **Job Description**

**You will join our Environment & Health** **department**

As our new Entry Level Air Quality Consultant you will be part of the Air & Climate Service Line within Ramboll’s Environment & Health Division. This group consists of like-minded individuals who are passionate about air and climate issues and assisting Ramboll’s clients with their most challenging problems. The Air & Climate team consults with clients across various industries on a range of topics, including but not limited to emissions estimation, air dispersion modeling, human health risk assessment, climate change, permitting, and compliance.

Your key tasks and responsibilities will be:

* + Preparing emissions calculations
  + Conducting air quality reviews of emissions reduction or control
  + Assisting in preparing major and minor source permit applications and environmental impact reports
  + Critically reviewing and interpreting local, state, and federal environmental regulations

  
**Qualifications**

**Your starting point for constant growth**

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

* B.S. or M.S. in Chemical, Mechanical, Civil, or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, or a science degree with air quality course work with a GPA of 3.5 or higher
* Strong computing skills including high level use of spreadsheets and word processing
* Strong written/verbal communication, problem-solving and organization skills
* Ability to understand and interpret environmental regulations
* Database and GIS skills are preferred but not required

  
**Additional Information**

**Welcome to our Environment & Health division**  
Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase live ability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

**Ramboll in the Americas**

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

**Salary Transparency Statement**

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $64,404 to $80,505 yearly. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

**Where People Flourish**

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

**How to apply**

Apply online. Atta

operational activities across UCLA. The incumbent provides technical consultation to the faculty, principal investigators,
  
researchers, staff, students, and campus departments regarding chemical, laboratory, and research safety requirements.

  

Responsibilities include developing and implementing Research Safety Management Plans; conducting lab hazard assessments
  
and compliance evaluations; developing and delivering safety training; participating in hazardous materials emergency response;
  
conducting incident investigations; supporting continuous process improvement initiatives; and performing other duties as
  
assigned.

  

Functional assignments may include support for research laboratories, engineering laboratories, medical and health sciences,
  
physical sciences, nanotechnology, hazardous materials, chemical hygiene, laboratory commissioning, laboratory design review,

Join an amazing team focused on advancing environmental justice across California.

Seeking someone who is enthusiastic about working with people, who is motivated to support California communities that face the greatest air pollution burdens, and who has excellent writing and organizational skills. This position is focused on, but not exclusive to Northern and Central California communities and requires occasional travel.

No two days look the same in this position. One day you might be analyzing monitoring data or writing a paper; the next, you're in a community meeting listening to residents describe pollution burdens in their neighborhood; the next, you're presenting policy recommendations to the Board.

This Air Pollution Specialist position (APS) plays a key role in implementing Assembly Bill 617 and advancing CARB's statewide strategy to reduce community-scale air pollution by working at the intersection of technical, scientific, legal, and policy topics in air quality. The Monitoring and Laboratory Division (MLD) is seeking highly qualified candidates to join the Operations and Data Support Section (ODSS) within the Air Monitoring Support Branch (AMSB). ODSS is responsible for administration and development of CARB's air quality data systems, including the Air Quality Data Management System (AQDMS), a digital datalogger (CARBLogger), and an information portal which support it's ambient air monitoring programs. ODSS also supports regulatory field operations by providing technical support of regulatory air monitoring instruments.

Under supervision of the Air Resources Supervisor (ARS 1) the APS in ODSS will administer and develop tools facilitating resource management, data management, data collection, and data validation of CARB's air quality data systems. The incumbent will coordinate with MLD staff, IT staff, and other stakeholders to unify MLD data systems. The incumbent will work with manufacturers and internal staff to evaluate and incorporate instrumentation into CARB's air quality systems by developing SOPS, procedures, and data workflows. The incumbent will provide training and technical support for field instrumentation and data systems.

Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
4+ years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.
MUST BE ABLE TO PASS an EPA background check to obtain access to US federal property.

Preferred Qualifications

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.
2-5 years of progressive experience in laboratories accredited for environmental analyses (e.g., TNI or NELAC, state programs).
Experience working at Federal facilities.
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) experience, knowledge of Promium Element LIMS is a plus.

Job Description And Duties

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters (SCHQ) in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

Under the supervision of an Air Resources Supervisor I, the successful candidate will carry out analyses of motor vehicle fuels using gas chromatography with flame ionization detector, supercritical fluid chromatograph, sulfur analyzer, x-ray fluorescence spectrometry, vapor pressure analyzer, and distillation analyzer. These analyses may be carried out at the SCHQ to prepare technical reports and scientific papers for presentation and publication and perform other duties as required. The candidate will also develop new test methods for the regulated fuel properties. Other duties include completing data and quality control reports, performing routine maintenance on the instruments, procuring supplies, managing service contracts, and developing new analytical methods or improving existing methods. An incumbent may also prepare and edit technical reports and scientific papers for publication and oversee the inventory and disposal of chemical reagents.

The position will be located at the National Space Science & Technology Center in Huntsville, Alabama, and will support the scientific development and application of satellite remote sensing products.

SPoRT is a NASA project to transition unique observations and research capabilities to the operational weather community to improve short-term forecasts on a regional scale. Based at the NASA Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, SPoRT is collaborating with the University of Alabama in Huntsville to provide direct science support along with science and technical coordination in the areas of weather, climate, air quality, natural disasters, satellite remote sensing, and data science and applications.

Duties/Responsibilities

Lead machine learning efforts in one or more of the following areas: air quality, wildland fire, and satellite remote sensing.
Provide scientific expertise to facilitate applied science studies in satellite remote sensing, health & air quality, or wildland fire.
Design higher-level value-added air quality products for applied science studies and manage data distribution to science investigators.
Develop synergistic products from TEMPO, ABI, and GLM data to enhance science applications, with special attention to wildfire smoke and lightning NOx.
Lead the development of new proposals and scientific papers on machine learning, satellite remote sensing, and numerical modeling.
Actively participate in and support SPoRT stakeholders through workshops, meetings, scientific conferences, and presentations of research results, including occasional travel to engage collaborators and end-users.

Minimum Requirements

Master’s of Science in Environmental Science, Meteorology, Atmospheric Science, Earth Science, Environmental Public Health, or a closely related discipline
Ability to perform satellite and geophysical data processing, analysis, and visualization (preferred experience would include the following sensors: TEMPO, MODIS, VIIRS, OMI, ABI, TROPOMI, EPIC)
Must have a strong programming background in Python and/or other programming languages.
Understanding of remote sensing theory, satellite data applications, air pollution chemistry, and meteorological principles
Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills
Willingness to work closely with others in a team environment
Desire to participate in science workshops and conferences, as well as in publishing results
Experience with machine learning techniques with satellite and/or model datasets and working with large datasets is desirable but not required for the position
U.S. citizenship is required

PhD is preferred

jobs.title: Executive Associate Dean, College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Executive Associate Dean is a senior academic leader and strategic advisor to the dean and a key member of the college's executive leadership team. Bringing the perspective and judgment of an accomplished faculty member and academic administrator, the Executive Associate Dean maintains a broad, integrated view of the college's academic programs, people, operations, partnerships, resources and priorities; identifies connections, opportunities and emerging issues across those areas; and provides strategic counsel to the dean on matters affecting the college and its long-term success.

Working closely with the dean, associate and assistant deans, department heads, center directors and other college leaders, the Executive Associate Dean helps translate college priorities into coordinated action and ensures that executive decision-making is informed by academic context, institutional knowledge and the perspectives of faculty and academic leaders. The position serves as a trusted advisor and sounding board to the dean, provides leadership on complex issues that span organizational and disciplinary boundaries, and represents and acts on behalf of the dean as appropriate.

In addition to this collegewide leadership role, the Executive Associate Dean provides executive oversight of academic operations, agricultural and commercial operations, facilities and land-use planning, and other designated areas of college operations.

Department Summary

The College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences (CAFES) at Cal Poly is one of the nation’s premier colleges of agriculture and natural resources – and the fifth-largest of its kind in the U.S. With more than 4,200 undergraduates, 16 majors, five graduate programs, and 192 dedicated faculty and staff, CAFES is a powerhouse of innovation, impact and hands-on learning. Our signature Learn by Doing philosophy comes alive across 10,000 acres of cropland, pastures, orchards, vineyards, and forests, as well as in specialized teaching and research facilities. From the Animal Health Center and Equine Center to the Center for Wine and Viticulture, Ag Tech Center and Plant Sciences Complex at the San Luis Obispo campus and Marine Transportation facilities at the Solano campus, students and faculty work side by side – tackling real-world challenges and shaping the future of food, agriculture and the environment. Discover more at cafes.calpoly.edu .

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with academic, administrative, industry and community audiences.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and institutionally across academic disciplines, programs and administrative functions.
Excellent leadership and management skills, including the ability to build alignment, develop others and lead through influence as well as formal authority.
A leadership style characterized by integrity, openness, flexibility, inclusiveness, transparency and kindness.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex and sometimes competing information and perspectives and translate them into sound recommendations for executive decision-making.
Demonstrated capacity to serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, including the judgment and confidence to offer candid counsel, constructive challenge and alternative perspectives.
Ability to move effectively between strategic and operational perspectives and recognize when an operational issue has broader academic, organizational, financial or reputational implications.
Record of successfully addressing complex issues that cross organizational, disciplinary or functional boundaries.
Demonstrated use of tact and diplomacy to effectively handle a broad range of high level and sensitive interpersonal situations with diverse personalities and to respond appropriately to conflicts and problems.
Ability to work well under pressure and maintain composure.

Education And Experience

PhD or terminal degree
Credentials appropriate for a tenured appointment at the rank of full professor within the College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
At least five years of relevant higher education administrative experience with evidence of increasing responsibility. Examples include service as an associate dean, department head or chair, program director or coordinator, center director, or leader of a sufficiently complex research or academic program.
Distinguished record of academic achievement and demonstrated effectiveness in teaching, research and service
Record of successful leadership of people, programs and complex initiatives
Demonstrated experience working across academic disciplines, programs or organizational units to advance shared priorities
Demonstrated understanding of faculty roles, academic culture, shared governance and the opportunities and challenges of leadership in a complex university environment
Commitment to collegial, collaborative and constructive interactions across the college and university

Licenses, Certificates, Credentials

Possession of a valid driver’s license or the ability to obtain by date of hire

Salary And Benefits

The anticipated hiring range for this role is $210,000 - $230,000. Note that the offer is calculated based on the background and relevant years of experience of the individual selected.

Factors in determining the appropriate compensation for a role include experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. The Anticipated Hiring Range referenced in the job posting is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position. The Classification Range may be broader than what the University anticipates paying for this position, based on internal equity, budget, and collective bargaining agreements (when applicable).

Cal Poly offers a best-in-class benefits program, including health, dental and vision insurance, retirement participation in the Public Employees' Retirement System, and educational benefits for eligible employees. See our benefits website for additional information.

About Cal Poly

Known for its Learn by Doing philosophy, Cal Poly is ranked among the top 10 public universities in the nation. Each year, more than 23,000 top-tier students come to Cal Poly in San Luis Obispo and Cal Poly Maritime Academy in Solano County to put knowledge into action, taking their learning outside the classroom as they prepare for careers in engineering, agriculture, science, business, humanities, maritime and the built environment. Cal Poly’s hands-on philosophy, small class sizes and close student-faculty mentorships result in graduates ready from day one to impact their communities, California and the world. For more information, visit www.calpoly.edu .

Working Within the California State University System

As part of the California State University, the nation's largest public four-year university system, Cal Poly employees contribute to a broader mission of advancing knowledge, creating opportunity and serving the people of California.

Watch: California State University Careers | Jobs, Benefits & Purpose

jobs.title: Principal Scientist, Toxicology
jobs.description:
Overview:

**ROLE AT A GLANCE:**  
The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will provide technical support in substantiating the safety of ingredients, formulas and packaging used in Herbalife inner and outer nutrition products in all stages of product lifecycle to support sustainable business growth. The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will work independently to conduct safety evaluation of ingredients, formulations and packaging, prepare appropriate documentation that meets standards and requirements for product safety and regulatory acceptability. This position will work closely with a wide range of regional and corporate teams across organization to ensure safety compliance of Herbalife products worldwide.

In addition, this position is expected to participate in external trade and science-based initiatives pertaining to the safety of product categories relevant to Herbalife business and leverage external partners to advance the science and brand of Herbalife products. The Principal Scientist is a key position in R&D and must inspire and energize employees through advanced knowledge of toxicology, personal leadership, influence, and thorough planning and drive for timely and appropriate results. This position may need to travel globally up to 10% of time.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT:**  

* Critically review, validate and summarize scientific evidence for assessing safety of proposed product formulas and materials (including food and dietary ingredients, additives, personal care ingredients, and their constituents) and provide recommendations to address evidence gaps (if any) to support product development and innovation with minimum supervision.
* Develop safety substantiation for Herbalife’s ingredients and finished products, and prepare written technical reports (e.g. risk assessments, safety monographs, etc.) that meet Herbalife internal standards and regulatory acceptability.
* Use published toxicological frameworks and regulatory guidance documents to perform and review hazard, safety and risk assessments to meet applicable regulatory requirements.
* Prepare responses to inquiries regarding the safety of Herbalife’s ingredients and products from regulatory bodies and customers in the local countries where Herbalife products are marketed.
* Lead and provide support in the design, conduct and evaluation of toxicology studies on existing and new ingredients and formulations with training.
* Lead stakeholder in preparation of requisite toxicological requirements for GRAS dossier preparation for North America and Novel Foods applications for Europe.
* Guide and review the development of safety-based specifications for raw materials and finished products, and advisory label statement review process.
* Communicate product and ingredient safety information verbally and in writing to internal customers, including Formulation, Scientific Affairs, Government Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and Post-market Safety Surveillance departments.
* Perform risk assessment and modeling of chemicals using established toxicological databases and tools such as OHAT systematic review, Benchmark Dose Software, Tox21, AOP and QSAR Toolbox under guidance.
* Remain abreast of current risk assessment methodologies and toxicological sciences relevant to Herbalife product categories and communicate emerging topics and potential implications to internal stakeholders.
* Represent Herbalife’s key business interests on trade association task forces, identify and pursue external Key Opinion Leaders for research collaboration opportunities, and support strategic external engagement with scientific and regulatory communities.
* Communicate critical issues to direct manager and other relevant parties in a timely manner, with recommended solutions including timelines and required resources.
* Follows Company policies, processes and procedures, and performs all duties in an honest, ethical and professional manner.
* Additional duties as assigned.

**LEADERSHIP AND SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* N/A

Qualifications:

**QUALIFICATIONS FOR SUCCESS:**

**Education**  

* Master or Doctorate Degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, or related discipline

**Experience**  

* 10 years of experience in toxicology research, nutrient risk assessment, food safety and/or personal care safety assessment areas. Experience gained before or after earning advanced degree will be accepted.
* Proven records of achieving positive results and adding recognized and quantitative value to business
* Successful track record of completing safety-based tasks including product/ingredient reviews
* Has achieved positive results and adding recognized and quantitative corporate value

**Skills/Certifications**  

* A broad knowledge of toxicology and its application to safety evaluation and risk assessment in food, supplements and/or personal care industry
* Working knowledge of toxicity testing methods and applicable regulatory standards
* Good understanding of emerging toxicological tools and risk assessment approaches
* Ability in interpreting, applying and translating complex scientific data (i.e., analytical and toxicological) for practical business use
* Ability to quickly acquire and apply new areas of scientific knowledge and share such information in a clear manner to a variety of stakeholders
* Ability to solve problems in a practical, timely and collaborative manner with adequate attention to detail
* Ability to work under pressure, adapt, navigate and thrive in a dynamic environment with changing priorities, and meet urgent deadlines
* Able to work in a team environment, including cross-functional and multicultural teams
* Solid communication skills, both written and verbal in English in all platforms
* Good project management skills, self-motivated and capable of working autonomously

Perform on-site sampling events as needed.

Maintain delivery truck to keep in proper working order.
Label samples after log in on an as needed basis.

Ability to lift up to 50 pounds. Samples will be in coolers packed in ice.

Basic computer skills.

Ability to read maps and follow directions
Ability to operate a motor vehicle
Ability to prioritize
Excellent communication (oral and written) and attention to detail
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude
Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, keep accurate records, follow instructions, and comply with company policies

### **Job Description and Duties**

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board (CARB) motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

  

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

  

Under the direction of the FAMES Manager, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist serves as an independent technical expert to oversee fuels analyses and methods. In addition, the incumbent will apply engineering principles to perform the more complex work of evaluating fuel effects on vehicle emissions and develop test methods for the fuel regulations when the need arises. Duties include evaluating and improving fuel analysis test methods; conducting fuel sample analysis; and overseeing the fuel analysis work conducted by other staff, conducting second-level quality control on reported data, reviewing literature studies related to fuel effect issues, and developing test plans to investigate fuel impacts. The incumbent will be responsible for data analysis, interpretation, reports, and oral presentations to stakeholders. The incumbent may also act as an expert witness for CARB or any related court action.

Clinical Training

jobs.title: Environmental Health Program Supervisor
jobs.description:
The Environmental Health Services Division of San Mateo County Health is seeking well-qualified candidates for the position of Environmental Health Program Supervisor.
Program Supervisors, under direction, supervise, direct, organize, manage, evaluate, audit, and provide accountability for one or more Environmental Health programs in the consumer protection (food, water, housing, vector control, land use, pools, solid waste, infectious waste, and cross connections) or hazardous materials/hazardous waste areas.

Currently, there are two regular vacancies in the Environmental Health Services Division's Consumer Protection Food/Pool Programs and Waste Programs. These positions are located in San Mateo, but will travel/drive throughout the county to perform the duties of the job.

The position in the Consumer Protection Food/Pool Program supervises staff that inspect food sold in markets, restaurants, schools, mobile catering facilities, and special events; educate the public and businesses about proper sanitation and food handling; follow-up on complaints and reports of food-borne illness; provide information on food establishment compliance; inspect public recreational water areas such as swimming pools/spas for health and safety compliance; and verify that businesses selling tobacco products have the appropriate permits.

The position in the Waste Programs supervises staff that inspect solid waste operations such as landfills, transfer stations, Post-Closure Landfill Development projects, medical waste generators, body art facilities and practitioners, and massage establishments. This position also supervises household hazardous waste collection operations for residents and small businesses and implements the County ‘s Safe Medicine Disposal Ordinance.

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board (CARB) motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills.
